title: Join A and B
description:
Given the sets `A = {19, 22, 24, 20, 25, 26}` and `B = {19, 22, 20, 25, 26, 24, 28, 27}`: Join A and B.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `join_sets(a, b)`, returning a SORTED list of the union of the two sets.
hints: "Joining" two sets means combining every element from both into one set, with duplicates collapsed automatically.
Python has both an operator and a method name for this operation - either one produces the combined set.
Use the | operator (or a.union(b)) to combine the sets, then return sorted(result).
expected_behavior: Returns a sorted list containing every element that appears in either set (the union), with no duplicates.
solution:
def join_sets(a, b):
    return sorted(a | b)
explanation: The | operator (equivalently, .union()) returns a new set containing every element from both operands, automatically collapsing any duplicates. Sorting the result gives a predictable order for checking.
